dispositions.method_decision: Do not add preload/friction or unused reinforcement credit. Existing 1224 end/case rows and 384 support domains remain usable components; no physical contact calibration or new native campaign is automatically required.
missing: Applicable interaction/allocation for captured axial forces, flange flexure/prying and seat contact consistent with the saved full actions.

dispositions.why_no_additional_scalar_comparison: The existing standard Cg, six-mode, common-work, steel and seat component comparisons are already executed. Multiplying their maxima or inventing a universal interaction would create a new unsupported criterion. Selecting an applicable complete allocation remains an engineering-method limitation, not absent raw forces or a request for another force solve.

missing: Applicable cross-grain timber-transfer resistance and interaction for the current local forces/moments, or supported complete reinforcement-and-anchorage allocation.
Complete retained-material transfer treatment at the two cleat/side groups outside the chosen common core; a conservative core exclusion is not missing physical wood.
Compatibility and baseline anchorage/heel/prying coverage for the existing header bridges; equilibrium and incremental strip resistance alone do not establish complete reinforcement.
dispositions.why_no_additional_scalar_comparison: The connected-parallel extension already addresses36 interrupted directions (216rows) within its scope; do not label all204 exclusions as unperformed available parallel calculations or subtract them as equivalent counts. The source-point census does not establish physical crack demand or pressure on retained material. No supported resistance is provided to turn its185 positive states into capacity ratios. No universal fracture/contact campaign is commissioned.

method_review.NDS_11_1_2: Member/local connection stresses require their own checks; Appendix E is one available method, not a universal whole-joint scalar interaction.
method_review.NDS_11_1_3: Eccentric cross-grain tension needs an appropriate engineering procedure or test. Passing lateral yield alone does not cover it; physical testing is not the sole route.
method_review.NDS_11_1_4: Mixed-fastener types need supported analysis/test basis. Wood/steel media alone are not different fastener types. Deferred Hillman resistance is not silently supplied by bolt checks.
method_review.NDS_11_1_5_and_11_2_3: Contact/fabrication assumptions and metal component failure modes remain separate from wood lateral reference values.
method_review.NDS_12_3_8: Adjacent-pair/three-member formulas have stated opposing-force and member-count scope. They do not authorize summing arbitrary asymmetric mixed-plane capacities. Detailed bearing/dowel analysis is an available alternative, represented only conditionally by the saved common-work constructions.
method_review.NDS_12_3_9: Two-member angled loading separates lateral capacity and axial bearing area; it does not dispense with an axial return path or arbitrary boundary moments. Shaft bending induced by lateral forces is already part of yield-mode mechanics and is not automatically a second independent load.
method_review.NDS_12_5_1: The smallest applicable end/spacing geometry factor propagates across the relevant group/shear planes. The principal 7D marker is not automatically the applicable factor for these oblique groups.
method_review.conventional_route_selected_for_this_eva: Retain saved component yield/bearing, member and geometry comparisons within their stated scope. Reject universal1/n as a whole-joint factor, plane-capacity sums, assumed permanent friction/preload and duplicated reinforcement credit. No complete adjusted multiaxial joint scalar is assigned where the supplied methods do not cover its boundary actions.
method_review.primary_scope: Retained 2024 NDS chapter PDFs read directly; no automatic claim about later editions or universal absence of an engineering method.
